model: Real allocated boards and scheduled engine playthroughs under the declared response-curve candidates. Three evidence classes kept separate: analytical envelopes (idealized growth against upgrade costs), already-acquired fixtures (the phenomenon rigs and the anonymized supplied-board reconstruction over declared finite level sweeps and declared synthetic reserve supplies), and fresh-start pacing (the scheduled prompt acquisition walk and the prompt purchase gesture, both real engine actions). A candidate is evidence toward the parent's coefficient decision, not approved tuning; no row is a 100-hour acceptance claim.

curves.description: rarity^level — the shipped exponential response progression, unmodified

curves.name: Linear
curves.description: 1 + 0.1·level — unbounded growth at one tenth of the authored share per level

curves.name: Bounded
curves.description: 1 + 3·level/(level + 20) — the explored bounded candidate, ×1 at level zero toward ×4 at infinite levels; a search candidate, not an approved coefficient

findings: Level-zero grant parity: every phenomenon board reads exactly the same rate under all three candidates at level 0 — the candidates preserve the shipped level-zero grants (tier rides every curve).
The amplitude-only control never moves: the candidates touch the Chorus/Exciter response grants alone — Booster, Field, and Spotlight legs read identically under every curve.
chorus-stack at level 1000: shipped 2.07e+174ν/s, linear 2.80e+79ν/s (shipped 7.4e+94× above it), bounded 3.22e+78ν/s (shipped 6.4e+95× above it).
exciter-producer at level 1000: shipped 1.12e+113ν/s, linear 6.39e+112ν/s (shipped 1.8e+0× above it), bounded 6.39e+112ν/s (shipped 1.8e+0× above it).
sideband-conversion at level 1000: shipped 1.27e+113ν/s, linear 7.86e+112ν/s (shipped 1.6e+0× above it), bounded 7.86e+112ν/s (shipped 1.6e+0× above it).
Supplied board at level 100: shipped 2.29e+72ν/s vs bounded 1.60e+27ν/s (shipped 1.4e+45× above); next-level marginal growth per ν 8.9e+45× shipped over bounded.
Supplied board at level 1000: shipped beyond the representable range vs bounded 1.21e+206ν/s.

Supplied-board waiting-time ratios across the level sweep (next level's cost/rate over this level's; above one means the next level takes longer) — shipped: 0.61, 0.29, 0.32, 0.33, —, —; linear: 0.73, 0.79, 0.94, 0.99, 1.01, 1.02; bounded: 0.69, 0.85, 0.97, 1.01, 1.02, 1.02. Both candidates cross above one inside the sweep and stay there; the shipped curve never does before its own board leaves the representable range.

5 envelope levels did not certify under the default budget (shipped@100, shipped@500, shipped@1000, linear@1000, bounded@1000) — their figures are the incumbent's, marked in the rows; the runaway board cannot even finish its own optimal search.
The supplied board's nine discovered undefeated enemies multiply every supplied row by 1.34e-1 — the reconstruction's absolute figures are pressured production, not unpressured capacity.
1 rows did not certify under the default budget and carry certified:false in place — supplied-board-p01-p30.

Fresh-start pacing is curve-invariant in this era: the scheduled prompt policy acquired no Chorus or Exciter within 12 days on seed 468, and the recorded acquisition scan agrees (seeds 0–11 at 20 days: 0 of 12 runs ever held a response support) — the candidates cannot move an opening era; the decision binds already-acquired boards.

The declared purchase-policy gesture sweep spends the same declared bank on the same already-acquired board under each candidate — the same levels land (the ladder's prices do not read the candidate), and the resulting-rate rows show what those levels do under each curve: the purchase side costs the same, the response side is what the decision changes.

Scope: these rows support choosing a structural candidate (which curve shape removes the runaway). They are not 100-hour progression acceptance; production adoption waits for the numeric-integrity tickets and calibrated era budgets.
